advances: One ordinary facet roof and its lifted escort centroid, plus a scalar curvature criterion for the full source density.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The inverse root is $\tau(P/\tau)^{(d+1)/d}$, the convex perspective of $r\mapsto r^{(d+1)/d}$. It is decreasing in the positive variable $\tau$ at fixed $P$. Since $P$ is affine and $\tau$ is concave, monotonicity and joint convexity prove convexity on the positive support.

The roof hypograph is convex. Taking its closure if needed changes only its boundary, which has zero $d$-volume. It is bounded: in positive facet dimension a relative interior point and its interior ball give, for every $x\in F$, a point in the ball on the opposite ray whose interpolation with $x$ is that interior point, with coefficient of $x$ bounded below uniformly. Nonnegativity and concavity then bound $\tau(x)$ by a fixed multiple of its value at the interior point. The zero-dimensional case is a single interval. The projective map preserves convexity on the positive chart because it maps each segment to the segment between the two images, with the parameter reweighted by positive denominators. Its $d$-Jacobian is $bP^{-d-1}$ by the rank-one determinant formula. Write the image as $(\xi,\eta)=(x,t)/P(x)$. On it $1-a_T\cdot\xi=b/P(x)>0$, so the image of $\ell\cdot x\ge c$ is $b\ell\cdot\xi\ge c(1-a_T\cdot\xi)$, independent of $\eta$. Integrating over each roof column gives the asserted pullback marginal.

Let $A=\int_F\tau P^{-d-1}$, $B=\int_F x\tau P^{-d-2}$, and $C=\int_F\tau P^{-d-2}$. The lifted base centroid is $B/A$ by the same Jacobian, and $A=bC+a_T\cdot B$ by the affine formula for $P$. Hence its inverse image is $bB/(A-a_T\cdot B)=B/C$. For example in $d=2$, $F=[-1,1]$, $\tau=1$ and $P=1+x/2$ give an escort mean strictly negative by pairing $x$ with $-x$, whereas the $\tau$-centroid is zero. The lift uses one continuous roof and carries no other facet or lattice labels.

For the derivative, write $N=d+1$ and $G=A_0s^{-N}+B_0$. Two differentiations give
$$
\frac{d^2}{ds^2}G^{-1/\beta}
=\frac{N A_0}{\beta}s^{-N-2}G^{-1/\beta-2}
\left[\left(\frac{N}{\beta}-1\right)A_0s^{-N}-(N+1)B_0\right].
$$
The prefactor is positive. Multiplying the bracket by $s^N$ gives the sign formula, and substituting $\beta=d$ and the coefficients gives the threshold. In particular when $E/V$ is near one the threshold is strictly below $s^{d+1}=1$, so a nonconstant affine denominator with values near one on an open facet patch gives negative second directional derivative there. Such denominators arise from small projective perturbations of a centered body: start with a centroid-zero body, apply the inverse map with a small nonzero parameter, and reversing its volume Jacobian gives zero gradient of the energy objective at the resulting affine denominator. Integrating the positive square of a nonzero linear functional against the second-derivative weight gives strict convexity, so that denominator is the attained optimizer. Choose a parameter with nonzero tangent component on the chosen facet.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $F$ be a compact convex set of dimension $d-1$ in facet coordinates, and let $\tau\ge0$ be a concave roof of positive integral there. The zero-dimensional integral uses counting measure at its point. Let $P(x)=b+a_T\cdot x>0$ on $F$ with $b>0$. The density $g=\tau P^{-d-1}$ has convex inverse $d$th root on its positive support. The $d$-dimensional convex hypograph $0\le t\le\tau(x)$ over $F$, mapped by $(x,t)\mapsto(x,t)/P(x)$, has uniform volume whose pullback marginal on $x$ is $b\,g(x)\,dx$. Vertical facet halfspaces map to ordinary halfspaces within the chart. Pulling the base coordinate of the lifted volume centroid back to $F$ gives
$$
x_*=\frac{\int_F x\tau P^{-d-2}\,dx}{\int_F \tau P^{-d-2}\,dx}.
$$
This center can differ from the $\tau$-centroid. For arbitrary $E,V>0$ put $A_0=1/((d+1)E)$ and $B_0=1/(d(d+1)V)$. For $s,\beta>0$, the sign of the second derivative of $(A_0s^{-d-1}+B_0)^{-1/\beta}$ is the sign of
$$
\left(\frac{d+1}{\beta}-1\right)A_0-(d+2)B_0 s^{d+1}.
$$
At $\beta=d$ its second derivative is nonnegative exactly for $s^{d+1}\le V/((d+2)E)$.
title: Projective facet roof lift and its escort center
